department: Department of Psychology — Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. (School of Science)

deadline.value: The application cycle for the Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. program opens September 1 and closes December 1.
deadline.quote: The application cycle for our Clinical Psychology and Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. programs opens September 1 and closes December 1.

gre_general.value: GRE scores are not required for the Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. program.
gre_general.quote: Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. program—GRE scores are not required.

gre_subject.value: GRE scores (including the Psychology Subject Test) are not required for the Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. program.
gre_subject.quote: Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. program—GRE scores are not required.

supervisor.value: The program notes that students work closely with a faculty mentor and invites prospective applicants to meet with faculty, but does not state whether a mentor must be secured before applying.

also.quote: You'll work closely with a faculty mentor, often in collaboration with other faculty on campus.

funding.value: Since 1994, all unconditionally admitted Addiction Neuroscience Ph.D. students in good standing have received full stipends and tuition scholarships for four to five years.
funding.quote: The Addiction Neuroscience program attempts to provide full financial support for all Ph.D. students throughout their graduate training, normally expected to last four or five years. entry_route.value: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution; a master's degree is not required to apply.
entry_route.quote: All applicants must have a bachelor's degree from an accredited institution (you do not need a Master's degree to apply).
